items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: So Reginald Forsythe, he showed me how to VOICE the trombones so they wouldn't -- I just added the part, and that's how I first learned how to space the brass out, from him.

ctx.x: when I was with Bernie Young, I used to go often across the street to the Metropolitan Theater to hear Erskine Tate's band, to listen to Omar Simeon because there was another great clarinet and great saxophone player. Because I always went to hear the saxophone players, mostly.

But anyway, I went to Chicago to play with Ralph Cooper in the Regal Theater, and by him bringing me from Minneapolis there, they fired the whole band off the job. So Ralph Cooper and Reginald Forsythe who was writing for Earl Hines, we were all cooped up together at the Oakwood Boulevard there, that hotel was called, I think, the Ritz -- the Tremier (PHONETIC) Hotel it was called then, right next to the Grand Terrace on Oakwood Boulevard.

So all the folks bunked up there together in this room. And so I had some arrangements and I had never written for over one trombone at that time. So I just took an ad, Earl Hines had two trombones. So I added another trombone part to my (SOPRANO SAX) (UNINTELLIGIBLE), took him over for Earl to play and they sounded terrible with this other added trombone part and I couldn't figure it out.
